property_summary: c.supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId, but the buggy version returns false for that input.

supportsInterface must return true for at least the IAccessControl interface ID (since the contract inherits both IAccessControl and ERC165) for any valid bytes4 input, but the buggy version fails to inherit ERC165's support and returns false for type(IERC165).interfaceId.
The reference always returns true for both type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and type(IERC165).interfaceId, while the mutant returns false for type(IERC165).interfaceId, breaking ERC165 conformance.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if and only if interfaceId is either type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the buggy version returns false for type(IERC165).interfaceId.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId (because AccessControl inherits ERC165), but the buggy version drops super delegation and returns false for that ID.

For any role and account, hasRole returns true if and only if the role was previously granted to that account via the public grantRole entry point by an authorized admin; the buggy version always returns false, breaking this invariant when a role has been granted.
After calling grantRole to give an account a specific role, hasRole returns true for that role and account; the buggy version always returns false, violating this guarantee.

For the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (0x00) which every address implicitly has according to ERC-7201, hasRole(0x00, any) must return true; the buggy M returns false unconditionally, breaking this even for the admin role.

For any role that has been granted to an account by the contract itself, calling hasRole with that role and account must return true; the buggy version unconditionally returns false for all calls, violating this rule once a role has been granted.
After the contract's own deploy-time setup grants a role to an executor, hasRole for that role and executor address must return true; the mutant always returns false.

For any role and account, calling c.hasRole(role, account) always returns the same boolean value as checking _roles[role].members[account]; the buggy version returns the opposite boolean for every role and account.

For any role and account, hasRole() must return the same value as an independent check using a granted executor role or the explicit setup roles; the buggy negation causes hasRole to report opposite membership for every call.

For any role and account, the return value of c.hasRole(role, account) must be opposite to the return value of c.hasRole(role, account) when called immediately after; the buggy negation makes two consecutive calls always return the same value.

For any role, account, and address that doesn't revert on a low-level call, a correct hasRole check must report false for an account that never had the role granted; the buggy negation makes it return true.

The admin role of any role returned by getRoleAdmin must equal the role's actual stored adminRole; the mutant always returns zero so a grantRole call from a non-admin address succeeds when it should revert.

For any role, calling getRoleAdmin(role) returns the same result as calling getRoleAdmin on that role's admin role recursively, reaching TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE as the ultimate admin; the mutant breaks this by always returning zero, which does not point to TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE.
For any role, calling getRoleAdmin returns a bytes32 that is itself a valid role (i.e., has a non-zero-length string representation or equals zero), but the mutant always returns bytes32(0).

For any role, getRoleAdmin(role) must return the actual admin role set via _setRoleAdmin, but the mutant always returns zero, so checking hasRole(getRoleAdmin(role), _msgSender()) for a role that has a non-zero admin will be false in the mutant while true in the reference when the sender holds that admin role.

For any role that has a non-zero admin role set, getRoleAdmin must return the actual stored admin role; the bug always returns DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (0x00), so the rule fails when the true admin is not 0x00.
For any role set via _setRoleAdmin, getRoleAdmin must return the admin role that was actually set; the mutant always returns DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, violating this when the set admin differs from 0x00.
